# Chapter 31 — Methodology: Pre-Registered Falsification with SHA-256, Exact p-values, Holm Correction and Shot Budget {#sec-qjax31 .unnumbered}

> **Día de análisis y actualización:** 23 de noviembre de 2026

> **Analysis and update date:** November 23, 2026

## 31.1 Register before measuring

A prediction is a closed dictionary (claim, metric, threshold, direction, $\alpha$, seed, date, script). It is serialized as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, UTF-8) and its SHA-256 is stored **in a commit prior to the measurement**. Verified with prediction `F-31-01` ("the $N$ mod 4 filter returns the ideal energy under uniform $T_1$", Ch. 28): the hash (`ec1f27a5b1d16582…`) does not depend on key order and **any** change in the 9 fields invalidates it (9/9). This is the part that prevents moving the threshold afterwards (`exact`). Limit: the hash proves that the text did not change, not that the commit predates the data; that is given by the date of the remote commit. The registration is a SHA-256 of a canonical JSON; it detects any later change to the claim, threshold or seed.

## 31.2 Deciding with an exact test

For "$p>p_0$" with $k$ successes in $n$ shots: confirmed if $P(X\ge k)\le\alpha$; refuted if $P(X\le k)\le\alpha$; otherwise **inconclusive** (not interpreted as support). With $p_0=0.5$: $P(X\ge60\mid n=100)=0.02844$ (confirmed), $P(X\ge530\mid n=1000)=0.03101$ (confirmed), $k=40$ (refuted), $k=55$ (inconclusive). The tails match `scipy.stats.binom` to $10^{-12}$ (`exact`).

## 31.3 Several predictions: Holm

With 20 null hypotheses and 3000 repetitions ($n=400$): without correction, $P(\ge1\ \text{false positive})=0.656$; with Holm–Bonferroni, **0.042** ($\le0.05$). This is why the protocol registers the complete **family** of predictions, not only those that turned out well (`exact`, simulation).

## 31.4 Shot budget

Detecting $p=0.6$ against $p_0=0.5$ ($\alpha=0.05$): $n=224$ for power $0.90$ (achieved $0.911$), $n=405$ for $0.99$. Detecting $0.52$: $n=5435$ ($\times24.3\approx(0.10/0.02)^2$): the cost grows as $1/\Delta^2$. A prediction that cannot reach power with the available budget must be registered as **untestable**, not as pending luck (`exact`).

Each measurement is reported with `qang.report.qang_report(counts, theta_qga, n_shots)` and its eight keys (`p0`, `qg_Z`, `m_qg`, `qga`, `qg_S`, `N`, `sigma_m`, `ci_95`), so preregistration fixes the estimator and interval as well (@sec-report01). In fields 28–31 the same report is labelled an information-theoretic analogue, not physical evidence.

## 31.6 Block (`qang/qfalsify.py`)

```python
def canonical(pred):                return json.dumps(pred, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
def register(pred):                 return hashlib.sha256(canonical(pred).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
def binom_upper(k, n, p0) / binom_lower(k, n, p0)
def decide(k, n, p0, alpha=0.05)    # "confirmed" | "refuted" | "inconclusive"
def holm(pvalues, alpha=0.05)       # Holm–Bonferroni
def shots_for_power(p0, p1, alpha=0.05, target=0.9)
```

## 31.7 Verification — `tools/verify_cap31.py`

```
[1] SHA-256 = ec1f27a5b1d16582…; order-independent; any change in 9/9 fields invalidates it
[2] P(X≥60 | n=100, p0=0.5) = 0.02844; decisions: confirmed | confirmed | refuted | inconclusive
[3] 20 nulls, 3000 reps: uncorrected 0.656; with Holm 0.042
[4] 0.6 vs 0.5: n=224 (power 0.911); n=405 for 0.99; 0.52 vs 0.5: n=5435 (×24.3)
verify_cap31: OK
```
The reproducible validation of this review is `verify_cap31: OK`: the SHA-256 is independent of key order and any change in 9/9 fields invalidates it; the binomial tails match SciPy to $10^{-12}$ and the decisions are confirmed/refuted/inconclusive; Holm lowers the FWER from 0.656 to 0.042 and the budget grows as $1/\Delta^2$ (224 → 5435); `tests/test_qfalsify.py` passes with `4 passed`.

### `tests/test_qfalsify.py`
```python
from qang.qfalsify import register, verify_registration, binom_upper, decide, holm
def test_registry(): p = {"a": 1, "b": "x"}; d = register(p); assert verify_registration({"b": "x", "a": 1}, d) and not verify_registration({"a": 2, "b": "x"}, d)
def test_pvalue(): assert abs(binom_upper(60, 100, 0.5) - 0.02844) < 1e-5
def test_decide(): assert decide(60, 100, 0.5) == "confirmed" and decide(40, 100, 0.5) == "refuted" and decide(55, 100, 0.5) == "inconclusive"
def test_holm(): assert holm((0.001, 0.03, 0.04)) == (True, False, False)
```

## 31.8 2026 context: certified shot windows

Status: `unverified` (read from the arXiv abstract only; nothing re-run). @finiteshot2026 compares symmetry verification and virtual distillation by finite-shot mean squared error with an explicit non-asymptotic remainder, and reports that no method wins in every regime.

| Question | Without `qang` | With `qang` |
|---|---|---|
| How many shots to decide? | rule of thumb | budget of §31.4 (`qang.qfalsify`), exact for the binomial test |
| Which mitigation method to pick? | compare by infinite-shot bias | unresolved: `qang` offers no certified window |
| Is the decision registered before measuring? | not necessarily | yes: SHA-256 and Holm (§31.1, §31.3) |

Scope: the `qang` budget answers how many shots decide a registered hypothesis, not which mitigation estimator to use; these are different questions and no gain over that work is claimed.
